requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale: I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.index.navigation`. I did not request implementation source. Each obligation in the requirement text maps to a marked test with assertions that enforce it. - **Badge links to its own anchored definition on the current page.** - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` asserts `id="habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}" href="#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}"` for a req, an example and a `.md`-containing name. - `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` asserts the same id/href pair. - `declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies` asserts both the anchor href and the alt text in the summary header, for both a req and a nested example. - **Separate adjacent arrow link to the evidence detail page.** - `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` asserts `title="View evidence" aria-label="View evidence for ..."` and the white arrow stroke. - `definition_evidence_link_targets_are_escaped` asserts the icon's `href` and `aria-label`, and that HTML special characters in the index path are escaped. - The repository test `mdbook_preprocessor_renders_definitions_between_stdin_and_stdout` asserts that each `habeas-definition-badge` span has an ``. That makes the arrow a separate adjacent link, tested through the real preprocessor binary. - **Arrow segment matches the badge color.** `definition_badge_and_evidence_icon_share_colors` extracts the badge color from the shields URL and the icon's background-color, and asserts they are equal for both a req and an example. - **One non-wrapping aligned row.** `definition_badge_stylesheet_keeps_the_arrow_in_one_row` asserts the wrapper declarations `inline-flex`, `align-items: center`, `flex-wrap: nowrap` and `white-space: nowrap`. It also asserts `flex-shrink: 0` on the links and the icon's centering and height declarations. Layout can't be rendered in a unit test, so asserting the CSS declarations is the reasonable check. The repository test confirms the wrapper span is emitted. - **No separate plaintext evidence link.** `!content.contains("See evidence")` is asserted in `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` and `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons`. - **Detail pages link back to the anchored definition and to the index.** - `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` checks `[Requirements index](../requirements-index.html)` on every detail page. It checks `[View definition](../rules.html#habeas-req-rules.cli%2Emdbook)` and the nested-chapter equivalent. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` checks both links on the `ready` page. - `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` checks the link for an example definition. - **Reference badges still link to the definition.** `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` asserts the `impl`, `cite` and `test` badges in a nested chapter carry `href="../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.ready"`. - **Links resolve when a name contains `.md`.** - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` asserts both link directions: `requirements.cli%2Emdbook.html`, and `../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.cli%2Emdbook`. - Several other tests assert the `%2Emd` form in the rendered output. I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.
